heading: Form 10-IEA: Why Business Taxpayers Can't Switch Regimes Annually
tldr: Taxpayers with income from a business or profession face restrictions on frequently switching between the old and new tax regimes.
To opt for the new tax regime, or to switch back to the old regime, these taxpayers must file Form 10-IEA.
Once an individual with business income opts out of the new regime, they can only re-opt into it once in their lifetime.
This restriction ensures consistency in tax planning for those with complex income structures.
The deadline for filing Form 10-IEA is typically the due date for filing your Income Tax Return (ITR).
caption:
Thinking about switching your tax plan? If you earn money from a business or profession, there's a special rule you need to know. You can't just jump between the old and new tax systems every year. There's a form (10-IEA) and a once-in-a-lifetime limit for switching back if you leave the new system. This helps keep things stable for your tax planning. Learn more about how this affects you.
